newsitem.title: FRANCE: Waigel optimistic on EMU budget pact accord.
newsitem.headline: Waigel optimistic on EMU budget pact accord.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he was "cautiously optimistic" about an agreement on an EU "stability pact" and said EU finance ministers would meet on Sunday to try to reach a deal.

"We hope we will be able to find a solution. We will meet next Sunday evening and I am hopeful we can reach an agreement then," he told reporters during a Franco-German summit in this western French town.

Speaking in German, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said he had nothing against the stability pact limiting budget deficits under monetary union but added it was not enough on its own and European people needed action on jobs.
"There are still two days to (an EU summit in) Amsterdam, I think it's possible to manage it," he said.

Waigel said attempts were being made to find a solution with a statement on employment based on articles 102 and 103 of the Maastricht treaty, which provide for intensified coordination of economic policies. "We are well on the way," he said.

Switching to French, Strauss-Kahn said, "We're going to work today and tomorrow and we're going to arrive in Amsterdam I hope with at least maybe an 80 percent agreement by....all the partners, not just Germany," he said. "Nobody wants more money. None of us have a lot of money to spend.
He said before going into further talks that "we have not finished working. Agreement was possible "this evening or in the next few days".
